Offline-first family messaging

Text your family when there's no signal.

CruiseMesh carries end-to-end encrypted messages between phones over the ship's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth — no internet package needed. It's built for cruise ships and anywhere coverage is unreliable — no accounts, no phone numbers, no tracking.

How messages get through

Messages are sealed on your phone and delivered by whichever route exists. Minutes of delay are expected and fine.

  1. Ship Wi-FiPhones on the same ship network find each other and deliver instantly, across the whole ship — no internet package needed. Some ships block phone-to-phone traffic; the app checks and tells you.
  2. Direct contactPhones within Bluetooth range exchange messages immediately.
  3. Data muleA family member's phone carries your sealed message until paths cross with the recipient.
  4. Internet deliveryWhen any one family phone gets online, it carries the whole family's sealed messages through a mailbox on the internet — needs a Cruise Pass or your own relay server.

Internet delivery

Your family gets a mailbox on the internet, and it's how one internet purchase covers everyone: when any single family phone gets online — one Wi-Fi package, a port-day café — it carries the whole family's messages to that mailbox and back, including to family at home who aren't on the cruise at all.

The mailbox holds sealed envelopes only — it can't read message contents, sender identities, or receipts — and deletes them after delivery or 30 days.

Run your own mailbox server on any small VPS, or skip the server admin with Cruise Pass — $9.99 for 30 days, one payment for the whole household, refundable no questions asked.

Private by design

  1. End-to-end encryptedMessages leave your phone as sealed envelopes. Relays and other phones never see plaintext.
  2. No accountsIdentity is a keypair generated on your phone. No email, phone number, or password.
  3. No trackingNo analytics, advertising, or crash-reporting SDKs — in the apps or on this site.

Details in the privacy policy.

Status

CruiseMesh is open source and in early development. Android (Kotlin) and iOS (SwiftUI) apps share a Rust core; store listings aren't public yet, so build from source for now.
